name: Tangerine Dream
hook: A West Berlin band who made the step sequencer, a machine that plays a pattern by itself, into the lead instrument.

blurb.age7: A band from Berlin who used a machine that plays notes over and over by itself, while they played on top.
blurb.age13: Edgar Froese started Tangerine Dream in West Berlin in 1967. In 1973 Christopher Franke bought a Moog modular synthesizer with money from their new deal with Virgin Records. It had a sequencer, a unit that plays a row of notes in a loop without anyone touching the keys. On Phaedra, released in 1974, that pulsing loop is the backbone of the music. It sold well across Europe and made Virgin a lot of money.
blurb.adult: Phaedra is often called the first sequencer album. That claim is loose. Sequencers were in use before it. It's safer to say it made the sequencer the centre of a hit record. The band's sequenced pulse runs forward into a lot of electronic music, and into film scoring through their own soundtracks from the late 1970s. Froese died in 2015, and the band continues without him.
